brief_extract:
THE ELECTRICAL AGE JANUARY 1959
Memorial to Dame Caroline Haslett
A Memorial Fund has been established in recognition of the great contribution made by the late Dame Caroline Haslett to many aspects of modern living, and to ensure that causes to which she devoted herself would be maintained. Dame Caroline’s earliest interest was in engineering; then in engineering applied to the home ; and then, through the domestic uses of electricity and the consequent saving of labour, in the contribution women could make to local and national affairs as housewives and as business and professional women.

brief_extract:
The Mansion House
By ALLEEN REYNOLDS, Corporation of London

THE Mansion House lies in the heart of the “square mile” of the City of London. Together with the Bank of England and the Royal Exchange, it dominates the busy Bank intersection where all roads leading to the City converge.

role: architect; Clerk of the City Works
brief_context: Architect who designed the Mansion House.
brief_extract: In 1728 the Court of Common Council set up a Committee to decide upon a site for building an official residence for the Lord Mayor, and having eventually chosen the site of the Stocks Market they opened a limited competition to well-known architects to submit designs. George Dance the ‘Clerk of the City Works’ was also ordered to produce plans and these were accepted by the Court of Common Council, and many people consider this to be Dance’s best work. The first Lord Mayor to occupy the Mansion House was Sir Crisp Gascoygne, who held office in 1752-53, but the building was not finally completed until 1758, and in that year the Easter Banquet—a ceremonial feast for distinguished guests held on the second Wednesday after Easter—was given in the newly completed Egyptian Hall.
